evidence: src/application/taskService.ts: getProject(projectId) does `const project = this.repository.projects.get(projectId); if (!project) throw new Error(`Project ${projectId} not found`)`. This is the module's own lookup abstraction.

src/application/taskService.ts: addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone and listTasks each repeat `this.repository.projects.get(projectId)` and the `Project ${projectId} not found` throw instead of calling getProject.
src/application/taskService.ts: assignTask and markTaskDone both repeat `project.tasks.find((t) => t.id === taskId)` and the `Task ${taskId} not found` throw, with no shared task-lookup helper.
src/application/taskService.ts: createProject/createUser write straight to repository.projects/users maps. This is consistent with the rest of the file and not a violation by itself.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is one file, src/application/taskService.ts. Its concern holds together: it is an application service for projects, tasks and users built on the injected domain Repository. The problem is that the file does not keep its own rules in one place.

The "project must exist" check is written out five times. Each copy does `this.repository.projects.get(projectId)` and then throws `Project ${projectId} not found`. The class already has `getProject(projectId)`, which holds exactly this check. `addTask`, `assignTask`, `markTaskDone` and `listTasks` don't call it. They read the repository directly, which bypasses the module's own abstraction.

The "task must exist in project" check is also written twice, in `assignTask` and `markTaskDone`. Each copy uses `project.tasks.find(...)` and throws `Task ${taskId} not found`.

If any of these checks changes, for example the error type, the error message or how the lookup works, every copy has to be updated by hand. The rubric's fail criteria cover exactly this: duplicating an invariant that should live in one place, and bypassing the module's own abstractions.

Having `createUser` in a TaskService is a small cohesion concern. It is reasonable because task assignment needs users, so it is not counted as a violation.

violations.message: The 'project must exist' check (repository.projects.get + `Project ${projectId} not found` throw) is written out in addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone, listTasks and getProject. The first four bypass the class's own getProject() abstraction instead of calling it.
The 'task must exist in project' check (project.tasks.find + `Task ${taskId} not found` throw) appears in both assignTask and markTaskDone instead of being kept in one helper.
